Title: Accept All Perils coverage with blank Comp/Specified Perils code and premium
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 1: Accept All Perils with blank Comp/Specified Perils data
Preconditions: Confirmed test policies are available. The authoritative coverage and premium fields are mapped to the current system. The test record follows the approved stored blank convention.
Test Data: Collision/All Perils Coverage Code = 40; Comp/Specified Perils Coverage Code = blank; Comp/Specified Perils premium = blank/zero according to the approved convention.
Test Steps: 1. Open or create a test policy. 2. Set Collision/All Perils Coverage Code to 40. 3. Leave Comp/Specified Perils Coverage Code blank. 4. Leave the Comp/Specified Perils premium blank or zero using the approved storage convention. 5. Save the coverage and submit it for validation.
Expected Result: The All Perils coverage is accepted. No conflicting coverage or premium validation error is produced. The saved effective coverage is consistent with the submitted values.

Title: Reject All Perils when Comp/Specified Perils coverage code is populated
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 2: Reject All Perils with populated Comp/Specified Perils code
Preconditions: The policy is eligible for coverage edit. The confirmed Comp/Specified Perils code list and UI/API field mapping are available.
Test Data: Collision/All Perils Coverage Code = 40; Comp/Specified Perils Coverage Code = one approved nonblank value.
Test Steps: 1. Open a test policy. 2. Set Collision/All Perils Coverage Code to 40. 3. Enter a populated Comp/Specified Perils Coverage Code. 4. Attempt to save or submit the policy. 5. Inspect validation feedback.
Expected Result: The system rejects or blocks saving/submission of the conflicting combination. The response identifies the All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils conflict. No conflicting GISA payload is sent.

Title: Reject All Perils with Comp/Specified Perils premium populated
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 3: Reject All Perils with Comp/Specified Perils premiums

Expected Result: The system rejects or blocks the conflicting premium data. The response identifies the affected premium or premium component. No GISA submission occurs while the premium remains populated.

Title: Reject All Perils with both conflicting code and premium
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data

Preconditions: The test policy is eligible for coverage edit and has both code and premium fields available.

User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 4: Server validation must apply outside the UI

Title: Prevent GISA payload containing conflicting Comp/Specified Perils code
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 2 and AC 4: Validate before GISA submission
Preconditions: GISA submission can be intercepted in a nonproduction environment. Persisted coverage contains All Perils code 40 and a populated Comp/Specified Perils code.

Test Steps: 1. Configure the test policy with All Perils 40 and a conflicting Comp/Specified Perils code. 2. Initiate GISA submission preparation. 3. Intercept or inspect the outbound payload. 4. Attempt submission.
Expected Result: GISA submission is blocked before transmission. The payload or validation log shows the conflict and the populated Comp/Specified Perils code. No external GISA acceptance of the conflicting payload occurs.

Title: Prevent GISA payload containing Comp/Specified Perils premium
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data

Preconditions: GISA submission can be intercepted. Persisted effective coverage has All Perils 40 and a populated Comp/Specified Perils premium.

Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 1: Blank code validation
Preconditions: The confirmed database/API convention allows NULL or an empty string for blank values. The test environment is isolated from production.
Test Data: Collision/All Perils Coverage Code = 40; Comp/Specified Perils Coverage Code = NULL.
Test Steps: 1. Insert or update the test record with a NULL Comp/Specified Perils code. 2. Ensure no premium is populated. 3. Run application validation. 4. Run the database relationship check.

Title: Use empty string as blank Comp/Specified Perils code
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 1: Blank code validation
Preconditions: The database/API schema permits an empty string representation for blank coverage code. The test environment is isolated.
Test Data: Collision/All Perils Coverage Code = 40; Comp/Specified Perils Coverage Code = empty string; premium = no populated value.
Test Steps: 1. Insert or update the test record with an empty-string coverage code. 2. Run application validation. 3. Run the database relationship check.
Expected Result: An empty string is normalized as blank and passes the rule. Whitespace-only values are not used as a substitute in this test.

Title: Treat whitespace-only Comp/Specified Perils code as blank
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 1: Normalize blank code values
Preconditions: The system has a confirmed normalization standard for whitespace. The field accepts or can receive whitespace in the test interface/API.
Test Data: Collision/All Perils Coverage Code = 40; Comp/Specified Perils Coverage Code = leading and trailing whitespace; premium = no populated value.
Test Steps: 1. Submit a Comp/Specified Perils code containing only whitespace. 2. Run coverage validation. 3. Inspect the normalized persisted value and validation result.
Expected Result: Whitespace-only input is normalized to blank or rejected under the approved whitespace convention. It does not incorrectly count as a populated conflict code.

Title: Validate approved zero premium convention
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 1: Confirm blank versus zero premium behavior
Preconditions: The business owner has confirmed whether zero is stored and whether it represents no premium.

Title: Verify premium recalculation does not recreate Comp/Specified Perils premium
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 3 and AC 4: Recalculate without conflicting premium
Preconditions: Policy is configured with All Perils 40 and no Comp/Specified Perils premium. The rating/recalculation process is available.
Test Data: All Perils code = 40; Comp/Specified Perils code = blank; no Comp/Specified Perils premium; trigger = approved recalculation action.
Test Steps: 1. Open or select the test policy. 2. Confirm the valid All Perils data. 3. Trigger policy premium recalculation. 4. Query the effective coverage and premium records. 5. Run GISA payload validation.
Expected Result: Recalculation does not create or retain a Comp/Specified Perils premium for All Perils. The All Perils premium remains governed by the approved rating process and no conflicting premium is submitted.

Title: Verify coverage change blocks GISA submission until conflict is resolved
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 2 and AC 3: Block GISA submission on invalid effective data
Preconditions: A controlled GISA environment and audit record are available. The test policy currently contains or can be updated to a conflicting combination.
Test Data: All Perils 40 plus populated Comp/Specified Perils code or premium.
Test Steps: 1. Configure a conflict in the effective policy data. 2. Initiate GISA submission. 3. Inspect validation and submission status. 4. Correct the conflicting code and/or premium. 5. Repeat validation and submission preparation.
Expected Result: Before correction the GISA submission is blocked. After correction the local relationship passes; GISA can proceed according to its separate approval process.

Title: Database query identifies invalid All Perils records
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Database and data validation context: query must return no valid records; conflict records require review
Preconditions: Database read access and confirmed policy/coverage table names are available. Effective-date and coverage keys are approved.
Test Data: One valid record with All Perils 40 and blank Comp/Specified Perils data; one invalid record with All Perils 40 and populated Comp/Specified Perils code or premium.
Test Steps: 1. Insert or identify records for both test combinations in the approved test schema. 2. Execute the confirmed relationship validation query using effective coverage keys. 3. Include PA106354437 and PA104948935 in the result set. 4. Review the record details.
Expected Result: The query returns only the invalid conflict record(s). The valid All Perils record is excluded. Results identify policy number, coverage code, premium/component, and effective date context.

Title: Database direct insert rejects All Perils conflict
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 4: Data integrity outside UI/API
Preconditions: Database test environment and an approved transaction are available. The implementation has an application guard, constraint, trigger, or documented direct-write restriction.
Test Data: Direct insert/update: All Perils code = 40; Comp/Specified Perils code = approved nonblank value; premium = approved nonzero value.
Test Steps: 1. Start a database transaction. 2. Insert or update the coverage data using the conflicting values. 3. Attempt to commit. 4. Roll back if the test environment permits. 5. Query effective coverage records.
Expected Result: The conflicting direct write is rejected or prevented by the confirmed database enforcement. If the implementation relies only on application validation, direct writes are blocked by platform policy and no conflict record persists.

Title: Database stores and audits All Perils correction
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Database audit and error context
Preconditions: Audit capture is enabled. PA106354437 has a record that can be corrected in the test environment. The confirmed audit fields and user/service identity are available.
Test Data: Before: All Perils 40 plus conflict data; After: All Perils 40 with blank Comp/Specified Perils code and no populated premium.
Test Steps: 1. Record the conflicting coverage and premium values. 2. Apply the approved correction. 3. Query coverage and audit records. 4. Confirm policy number, effective date, previous value, corrected value, source operation, timestamp, and GISA context.
Expected Result: The corrected effective record contains All Perils 40 with blank Comp/Specified Perils code and no populated premium. The audit trail records the changed values and operation without removing unrelated coverage.

Title: Validate only effective coverage records, not unrelated historical rows
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Database and data validation context: compare effective policy/coverage period
Preconditions: The test policy has both current and historical coverage records. Effective-date keys and transaction keys are confirmed.
Test Data: Current effective record: All Perils 40 with blank Comp/Specified Perils data. Historical record: approved historical values that are outside the current effective period.
Test Steps: 1. Identify effective coverage keys for PA106354437. 2. Execute validation using the effective policy/change context. 3. Repeat using a historical context if supported. 4. Compare submitted payload data with the effective database record.
Expected Result: Only the effective record controls current validation and GISA payload generation. Unrelated historical records do not cause a false current conflict.

Title: Database check excludes unrelated policies
User Story: Story 1 - Prevent conflicting All Perils and Comp/Specified Perils coverage data
Acceptance Criteria: Story 1 AC 5: Policy scope and unrelated policy regression
Preconditions: At least two test policies exist: PA106354437 and PA104948935. A separate unrelated policy has conflicting or valid but nonmatching data.
Test Data: Include PA106354437 and PA104948935 in the review set; include an unrelated policy outside the review list.
Test Steps: 1. Run the policy conflict query for PA106354437 and PA104948935. 2. Run or compare a scope query that includes an unrelated policy. 3. Correct and requery both identified policies. 4. Confirm no unrelated policy is changed.
Expected Result: The identified-policy query reports only the approved in-scope policies. Remediation updates PA106354437 and PA104948935 as applicable without changing unrelated policies.
